subject: Acme Health: streaming endpoint p99 spikes during peak - urgent escalation
messages:
From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Park <kyle@chatly.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 14:12:03 -0800
Subject: [Urgent] Streaming chat p99 spikes during tonight's peak (Feb 11)

Vanessa —

We're seeing a serious spike in tail latency on the streaming chat endpoint (SSE/WebSocket) during our evening peak. P95 seems OK (~220ms) but p99 jumped to 4.2s+ starting ~18:00 UTC and persisted for roughly 30 minutes; it happened again in the next window. Conversations dropped and our UX shows long hanging "typing" states.

Attached are a small set of logs and a short trace bundle from our client side that show multiple RTTs and stalled frames. We rely on streaming for our live triage workflow and this behavior is causing support pages to fill up. This is hitting PROD (site: acme-prod).

Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing platform-side regressions? We need immediate triage and — if this is on your side — a plan for workaround or mitigation. Please advise if you need us to route traffic away or enable a non-streaming fallback temporarily.

We are also going to open a ticket internally but wanted to loop you first. This is disrupting our scheduled care sessions.

Thanks,
Maya Chen
Head of Product
Acme Health

Attachments: acme-sse-logs-20270211.tar.gz (text tar), trace-snippets-14-16.json (json)

What we're doing now:
- I've looped in SRE (Dylan) and our CS lead (Marissa).
- SRE will pull platform traces for the windows you indicated and check autoscaler events and batching/queue depth.
- If we confirm a platform-side regression we will propose an immediate mitigation (routing to burst capacity or a temporary non-streaming fallback) and a credit action.

Could you confirm the last affected conversation IDs and whether disabling streaming for a single region (us-west-2) is acceptable? If you prefer, we can flip traffic to the REST polling endpoint for a short window while we stabilize.

We appreciate the attachments — SRE will review. I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until we have a root cause.

-Vanessa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 14:38:17 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Acme streaming p99 spike preliminary triage

Folks — quick initial notes from the triage window (14:30 local):

Observations:
- Platform metrics show a correlated spike in request queue depth at the SSE frontends and a simultaneous rise in per-connection tail latency (p99) across us-west-2.
- Autoscaler activity shows delayed allocation events (nodes became healthy ~45–70s after scale triggers) during that interval; we saw up to 3x queued batches for long-tail conversations.
- The affected model variant had a recent quantization patch rolled out in the last deploy window (02/10). Kernel selection stats show a fallback path that increases per-token compute for long contexts; hypothesis: an edge case in the quantized kernel causing increased per-token time under bursty parallelism.

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Route Acme traffic to dedicated burst pool (requires ops approval, will increase cost but minimal customer impact).
2) Force smaller batching window / throttle concurrency for their org (fast to apply, may increase overall token cost and reduce throughput).
3) Flip to non-streaming REST path for high-latency conversations (client work required, but stable).

I pulled snippets and attached a small trace bundle (trace-snippets-14-16.json). Logs show stalled decode loops; correlates with kernel fallback counts. My ask: approval to route to dedicated burst pool for 60 minutes while we revert the quantization kernel change and run a controlled rollout. Also recommend we prepare a goodwill credit while we investigate.

Dylan
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: trace-snippets-14-16.json
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/acme-sse?from=1676187120000&to=1676194320000

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 15:02:05 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Streaming chat p99 spikes during tonight's peak (Feb 11)

Maya — quick update and two proposed short-term paths.

Update:
- SRE has identified queued-batch and kernel-fallback signals that line up with your incidents. We're investigating a recent quantization kernel change.

Proposed short-term options (pick 1):
A) We route your traffic into a dedicated burst pool for the next 60 minutes. This reduces likelihood of queuing and keeps streaming semantics. Ops will need signoff (we're asking now).
B) We flip higher-latency conversations to the non-streaming REST endpoint for 30 minutes; no code change on your side if you accept minor UX degradation (slightly larger payloads, no incremental tokens).

Which do you prefer? If you tell us now we can action within 5–10 minutes. We're prepared to issue a goodwill credit depending on impact; Vanessa will advise on that track.

-Marissa
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Kimberly —

Summary: Acme Health (DEAL-7832) experienced repeated p99 tail-latency regressions on the streaming chat endpoint during peak windows on 2027-02-11. SRE has a preliminary root cause pointing at a quantization kernel fallback path introduced 2027-02-10. The issue caused user-visible stalls for their care-workflow and is currently being actively mitigated.

Requested executive approvals:
- Approve short-term routing of Acme traffic to a dedicated burst pool for 60 minutes (immediate ops action). This will be billable but we will absorb cost for goodwill if you'd like to offer a credit.
- Approve a goodwill credit up to 10% of Feb usage for the impacted window pending final impact analysis (we expect to finalize by Monday).

Attachments: grafana-p99-20270211.png (screenshot), acme-sse-logs-20270211.tar.gz (client logs)

Impact: high (customer-facing, scheduled care sessions degraded). If we don't move fast the customer has indicated they will escalate to procurement / pause new launches.

Please reply with a one-line approval ("approve capacity burst" / "approve credit up to X%") so I can action with Ops and CS.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
